correctness.rationale: For odd n=2m+1, alpha=pi/n, c=cos(alpha), s=sin(alpha), area(P)=nsc. For the edge from (c,-s) to (c,s), normals from edge interiors meet the polygon in the strip |y|<=s. The upper omitted cap has vertices v_0,...,v_(m-1), q=(-1+s²/c,s) on the final edge, with shoelace area 2C=(s/c)(2(m-1)c²-2c+1); the lower cap is congruent. This yields U_E=(s/c)(3c²+2c-1). Hann planar identity, reproduced in Domokos--Langi Remark 1, equates total vertex and edge active areas, giving mean=2n U_E/(nsc)=6+4/c-2/c²=8-2(sec(alpha)-1)² for all odd n>=3. Since sec(pi/n)-1 decreases with n and sec(x)-1=x²/2+O(x⁴), the claimed strict increase, n=3 value 6, and quartic asymptotic follow. An independently written clipping code matched formula for odd n=3,5,7,9,11,13,17,31,51,101 to ~1e-14 and a 100,000-interior-point Monte Carlo face-normal census corroborated n<=17. These finite checks are not the general proof.
residual_risks: The proof relies on Hann planar Euler-type identity as reproduced in a later inspected primary paper; the original 1993 article was inaccessible.
RESULT.md final asymptotic math display contains a literal form-feed character instead of backslash-frac; this is a formatting defect, not a failure of the stated mathematical theorem.

evidence: Hann planar identity as reproduced by Domokos--Langi: sum_v area(U_v)=sum_E area(U_E). It yields n(P)=2 sum_E area(U_E)/area(P) but does not evaluate individual edge-strip area.
Hug cyclic centrally symmetric equality n(P)=8 applies to even regular polygons and does not entail n(P_n)=8-2(sec(pi/n)-1)^2 for odd n.
The triangle special case n(P_3)=6 in Nasonov--Panina--Siersma is already covered by their result, while the n>=5 all-odd-n family and quartic asymptotic are not entailed by that isolated case.
Independent polygon cap-area evaluation U_E=(sin(alpha)/cos(alpha))(3cos²(alpha)+2cos(alpha)-1), n=2m+1, supplies the extra computation linking the general identity to the new family.

value.rationale: The mean number of boundary normals is a natural classical Santaló invariant. Odd regular n-gons form the canonical non-centrally-symmetric counterparts to even regular polygons known to have mean 8. The exact full-family computation identifies a nontrivial quartic deficit 8-mean=pi^4/(2n^4)+O(n^-6), supplying a rigorous benchmark for planar extremal investigations. It is not a table recomputation or a trivial substitution: it requires evaluating active strip geometry for all odd orders. This does not resolve whether arbitrary convex bodies can have mean >8.
residual_risks: Value pertains only to Euclidean regular odd polygons and the average-normal invariant, not all convex polygons.
